clue.text: Confucius he say he write the Chinese one

definitions.text: Confucius he say he write the Chinese one

parts.words: Confucius he say he write the Chinese one
parts.note: a mock-pidgin Confucius saying: the books Moses is held to have written, five in all, matched against the Chinese classic Tao Te Ching, which the name half sounds like

explanation.surface: A joke in the style of a Confucius saying about a Chinese sage writing a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Pidgin 'he write' points to the tradition that Moses wrote the five books of the Torah, and 'the Chinese one' to the Tao Te Ching, whose first syllables the Greek name loosely echoes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek name for the five books of Moses, the opening of the Hebrew Bible.

clue.text: Job at Bukowski's office

definitions.meaning: a job or appointment is a position held
Charles Bukowski's first novel is titled with this word followed by Office

explanation.surface: Someone works a job in the office of the American writer Bukowski.
explanation.definitionFit: A post is a job, and Bukowski's novel about his years as a mail carrier is called Post Office.

clue.text: Dwarf the last name of French composer brothers

definitions.meaning: the French word for a dwarf

definitions.text: the last name of French composer brothers
definitions.meaning: the brothers Le ..., three seventeenth-century French artists, share this surname

explanation.surface: A small person bears the surname of a family of French brothers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Le Nain brothers were in fact painters rather than composers; the clue's 'composer' is best read loosely as 'artist'.
explanation.definitionFit: In French a dwarf is nain, which is also the surname of the Le Nain brothers.

clue.text: Would Powell's characters ever wear morning or evening dress?

definitions.text: Would Powell's characters ever wear morning or evening dress?

parts.words: Would Powell's characters ever wear morning or evening dress?
parts.note: Anthony Powell's first novel is named after its idle young people; the joke is that men named after the middle of the day would wear neither morning dress nor evening dress

explanation.surface: A question about whether Anthony Powell's characters dress formally.
explanation.definitionFit: Powell's 1931 novel about bored young Londoners bears this title, a phrase for men of leisure.

clue.text: Pal Joey

parts.note: John O'Hara's Pal Joey stories and the musical made from them have a nightclub singer called Joey as hero; this is his surname

explanation.definitionFit: Joey Evans is the full name of the hero of John O'Hara's Pal Joey.

clue.text: Ellis was one, Felix Krull another

definitions.text: Ellis was one, Felix Krull another

parts.words: Ellis was one, Felix Krull another
parts.note: Thomas Mann's novel is the Confessions of Felix Krull, and Ellis is another writer of confessional memoir, so each is a teller of confessions

explanation.surface: Two figures from literature are said to belong to the same class of person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes confessions, as the hero of Mann's Confessions of Felix Krull does.

clue.text: Final notice

parts.note: read as the last newspaper notice a person ever receives, the death announcement, rather than a last reminder of a bill

explanation.definitionFit: A short form of obituary, the newspaper report of a death, the last notice anyone gets.

clue.text: Fast be able, perhaps, to produce a tale by La Fontaine

indicators.note: perhaps says the words before it are one possible arrangement of the letters needed

explanation.surface: A suggestion that being quick might help you write a story like La Fontaine's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals rearranging FASTBEABLE; 'to produce' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: La Fontaine wrote fables in which animals act out moral lessons, the classic kind of animal tale.

clue.text: Kind dog for compositor

parts.note: a kind or sort is a type
a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: A breed of dog is suggested as suitable for a printing worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A compositor sets type by hand for printing, the old trade name for this job.

clue.text: Composer awkward as ten in crack unit

indicators.note: awkward suggests the letters of the words are clumsily arranged and need putting right

parts.note: the SAS (Special Air Service) is the British Army's elite regiment

explanation.surface: A composer is having an awkward time in a military crack unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' scrambles the clue's letters together with the regiment's; the surface's 'in' looks like a container signal but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Camille Saint-Saens was the French composer of The Carnival of the Animals.

clue.text: Practitioner holds a right to Irving hero

indicators.note: holds means the doctor's letters wrap around the other pieces

parts.note: GP is short for general practitioner, a family doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor keeps a right that belongs to one of John Irving's heroes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts A and R inside GP; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Garp is the hero of John Irving's novel The World According to Garp.

clue.text: Tip never refused by her

parts.note: in Dickens's novel the heroine's feckless brother is nicknamed Tip, and she always gives in to him; the surface suggests a gratuity never turned down

explanation.surface: A woman who never refuses a gratuity.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's heroine Amy Dorrit, nicknamed this, indulges her ne'er-do-well brother Tip.

clue.text: Thrice great Neoplatonist

definitions.meaning: the Greek epithet means three times great
Hermes, the legendary author of the Hermetic writings prized by Neoplatonists, bears this epithet

explanation.surface: A Neoplatonist philosopher praised three times over.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermes Trismegistus, the supposed author of Hermetic texts, carries the Greek epithet meaning thrice greatest.

clue.text: Christopher Robin, possibly, or Sebastian Flyte

definitions.text: Christopher Robin, possibly, or Sebastian Flyte

parts.words: Christopher Robin, possibly, or Sebastian Flyte
parts.note: both are famous for a teddy bear, Pooh and Aloysius, so each is a lover of bears

explanation.surface: Two literary figures, A. A. Milne's boy and Waugh's Oxford aesthete, linked by a hobby.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek-built word for a lover or collector of teddy bears, as both characters are.

clue.text: Like the Herald in wartime

parts.note: Stentor was the herald of the Greeks in the Trojan War, whose voice was as loud as fifty men; the surface suggests a newspaper called the Herald

explanation.surface: A newspaper called the Herald shouting its headlines in wartime.
explanation.definitionFit: Stentorian means very loud, after Stentor, the bellowing herald of the Iliad.

clue.text: Some of play recreating the past (operates backwards)

parts.note: retro style imitates fashions of the past
acts are divisions of a play

explanation.surface: Part of a play that looks back to former times.
explanation.definitionFit: To retroact is to take effect on past events, working backwards in time.

clue.text: The whole baronetage, peerage, — of England" (Thackeray, Vanity Fair)

definitions.text: The whole baronetage, peerage, — of England" (Thackeray, Vanity Fair)

parts.words: The whole baronetage, peerage, — of England" (Thackeray, Vanity Fair)
parts.note: a fill-in quotation: Thackeray lists the ranks of English society, ending with the common people below the titled

explanation.surface: A quotation from Vanity Fair with a word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Commonage is an old word for the common people, the ranks below baronets and peers.

clue.text: Pamphlet reportedly followed

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is heard rather than written, so we want what sounds like it

parts.note: to have followed someone is to have tracked them

explanation.surface: A leaflet is said to have been pursued.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political.

clue.text: Curtains raised by him in 1961

parts.note: the theatre critic Kenneth published his collection of reviews called Curtains in 1961; the surface suggests a stage curtain going up

explanation.surface: A man raised the theatre curtains in 1961.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenneth Tynan, the drama critic, published Curtains in 1961.

clue.text: Smile Lear contrived in French port

indicators.note: contrived means artificially arranged, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: King Lear forcing a smile in a French harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Marseille is France's chief Mediterranean seaport.

clue.text: Introduction in favour of educational toy followed by fellows accepting negative

indicators.note: followed by places the next pieces after the ones before

parts.note: pro means in favour of
Lego is the building-brick toy

indicators.note: accepting means one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: men are fellows
no is a negative answer

explanation.surface: An introduction recommending a building toy to men who say no.
explanation.definitionFit: A prolegomenon is a preliminary essay or preface to a book.

clue.text: Rousseau on education? or Zola?

definitions.meaning: Rousseau's treatise on education is named after its pupil
the first name of the French novelist Zola

explanation.surface: Was it Rousseau who wrote on education, or Zola?
explanation.definitionFit: Emile is Rousseau's treatise on education and also the first name of the novelist Zola.

clue.text: A boat for Crane, several for Noyes

definitions.text: A boat for Crane, several for Noyes

parts.words: A boat for Crane, several for Noyes
parts.note: Stephen Crane wrote the short story The ___ Boat, and Alfred Noyes is credited with a book of such boats; the surface reads like crane and boat hire

explanation.surface: One boat for a crane to lift, several for someone called Noyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Crane's famous story is The Open Boat, about castaways in a dinghy.

clue.text: Governess to inspect around river

indicators.note: around means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: to eye something is to inspect it

explanation.surface: A governess is told to look over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Eyre, Charlotte Bronte's heroine, works as governess at Thornfield.

clue.text: Seen as pre-Murdoch in the world of communications

definitions.meaning: the name that comes before Murdoch, the novelist's first name
the Greek messenger goddess of the rainbow

explanation.surface: The media world before Rupert Murdoch arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Rupert Murdoch the media owner; the writer meant is the novelist Iris Murdoch.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is the novelist Murdoch's first name and the messenger goddess of Greek myth.

clue.text: "Blissful language" is coming back with diagram in remuneration

indicators.note: in means the pieces go inside the payment

parts.note: remuneration is pay

indicators.note: coming back means the little word is read backwards

parts.note: a graph is a diagram

explanation.surface: Happy talk returns with a chart in someone's wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns IS into SI; 'with' is a link. Bliss symbols, Charles Bliss's picture writing, are an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A universal written language of symbols, such as Blissymbolics devised by Charles Bliss.

clue.text: So, big writer seen with new dean

indicators.note: new says the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A big writer is seen with a newly appointed dean.
explanation.walkthrough: Edna Ferber won the Pulitzer Prize for her novel So Big; 'seen with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna Ferber wrote the novel So Big.

clue.text: A tender Sprite, pace Wordsworth

parts.note: Wordsworth's Pastoral Ballad on this subject calls the feeling of remorse a tender sprite; pace means with respect to him

explanation.surface: A gentle fairy, as Wordsworth might put it.
explanation.definitionFit: Repentance is sincere regret for wrongdoing, personified by Wordsworth as a gentle spirit.
